purpose: Test whether a visual reviewer can locate known failures and state the visible condition required to clear each failure.
countercondition_notice: A pass countercondition is a review distinction, not a positive design example or a reusable visual direction.

pairs.expected_failure: The copper ring collides with and crowds the green module without a source-backed purpose.
pairs.pass_countercondition: The elements are clearly separated, or the overlap is intentional, source-backed, readable, and safe at every tested size.

pairs.expected_failure: The lower modules do not follow a clear shared alignment or responsive relation.
pairs.pass_countercondition: The modules follow a clear optical relation at wide, narrow, sub-320, zoomed, and rotated states without overflow or lost content.

pairs.expected_failure: The display headline dominates while the small labels carry unclear information and weak reading support.
pairs.pass_countercondition: Type size, measure, spacing, and rank support the task, preserve all required text, and remain readable in every tested state.

pairs.expected_failure: The line symbols imply operational meaning that the source and visible content do not establish.
pairs.pass_countercondition: Each symbol has an explicit source-backed role and visible relation to its content, or the unsupported symbol is omitted.

pairs.expected_failure: The board names restaurant operations but shows no status, workflow, timing, role, inventory, or exception relation.
pairs.pass_countercondition: The composition makes at least one source-specific operational relation visible and testable instead of relying on a title.

pairs.expected_failure: The paper grid, earthy palette, serif italic headline, swatch strip, and oversized geometry repeat a familiar brand-board formula.
pairs.pass_countercondition: The visual system follows distinct source relations and loses important meaning if moved unchanged to an unrelated source.
